P1.evidence: No reference to the setter's notes or the application at any point. Frame was three parts, not four: 'go a little bit into what you actually want to achieve, where you're currently at, see if we can help with that. If we can, I'll take you through how, okay?' — no 'what's in the way' or 'what you need'. Agreement obtained ('Okay, sounds good'). Opening question was narrowed to the physical rather than the open 'what are you potentially looking for help with'.

P2.evidence: Weight, height and age asked directly at 00:11:45 (190 lb, 5'8", 29). Occupation was volunteered inside the goal answer, not asked; the rep only probed shift length much later ('you sometimes have like 24 hour, 48 hour sessions, right'). Health conditions and hereditary history never asked. Injuries asked ('do you have like any injuries, some sort of aches') but duration never asked. Training week captured fully. Results from current training were volunteered ('Even in the little bit of time that I've done kettlebells, I've seen growth') and never asked for. Nutrition asked properly. Sleep and daytime energy never raised.

P3.evidence: Strength, endurance, mobility and flexibility all surfaced and scaled 1-10. The bridge question was asked verbatim in substance — 'is there anything outside of the physical aspect that you're also trying to achieve, maybe something like confidence' — but the prospect said no and the rep dropped it instead of going deeper. No 'who else does that impact', nothing about family, identity or legacy despite an obvious opening (firefighter, colleagues, job capability). Reflect-backs were frequent and accurate but stayed at the level of the goal list; the 'this isn't really about X, it's about Y' reframe never came.

P4.evidence: Asked how long he had wanted this and why he had not done it — got 'I don't like traditional lifts. So just, I haven't really had the route to achieve that goal' — but never asked what he had actually tried or what happened with it. The prospect named the gap himself: 'I'm having to come up with these workouts myself, and I don't know if what I'm doing is perfect... I think I'm much less likely to put in the effort if I continue the way that I have been doing it.' The rep converted this into an accountability frame with the Kobe Bryant / pro-athlete-has-a-coach analogy, which is a weaker variant of the 'why can't you stick to it on your own' move.

P5.evidence: Consequence question asked and then re-asked when deflected: 'what would that eventually result to for you if you don't make those changes there?' The prospect batted it away — 'Look, if I put in the work, I know I'm going to get better... I highly doubt that this won't work if I put in the effort' — and the rep never landed a cost of inaction. No 'willing to settle for that', no 'why not', no line in the sand. The consequence frame was the weakest phase and it is the reason the close had no leverage when price landed.

P6.evidence: Belief check run as a 1-10: 'where one is like, Richard, I don't really see this working for me. And 10 is like, yeah, seems good' — answered nine, with the reservation 'I haven't seen the app and I haven't seen how all these different calls go'. The rep asked the good down-scale follow-up ('Why not like a seven or six?') but never ran the all-in commitment question, and moved to price with the reservation unresolved.

P11.evidence: Payment collected live — the rep sent a join link in chat and stayed on while the prospect paid ('I'm to do that 200 a month'). No Trevor onboarding call exists for the product actually sold, so step 2 is unreachable. No agreement email confirmed and nothing signed on the call. Skool access was walked through on screen including the level mechanic, but there was no welcome email, no onboarding questionnaire, and the rep substituted his own personal WhatsApp number and a self-booked 15 July check-in.

objection_plays.detail: The isolate was attempted in weakened form — 'Outside of the investment, do you feel like I do want to do this?' — and got a yes. Nothing after that ran: no 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place', no 'most clients pay upfront, but for some we break it up', no permission question for an honest financial conversation, and none of the six financial-picture steps (cash on hand, monthly surplus, number of cards, available credit, used vs available, investments). Payment plans were raised and dismissed by the rep himself in one sentence: 'The only thing I was thinking that we could have done was maybe split it up into a few pairs, but of course that's not going to change the $2,000 number.' Roughly ninety seconds after the objection landed the rep was quoting a different, cheaper product. The rep conceded the failure to his manager the same day: 'He told you? Did you open wallet him?' / 'I did not.'

SCRIPT GAP: the playbook has no path for the reduced-scope downsell the rep reached for. There is no scripted qualification for who should be offered the $200/month membership, no rule that the open wallet must be exhausted first, and no guidance on which tier of it to present — the rep did not know the $2,000/12-month option existed and put a prospect whose stated ceiling was exactly $2,000 onto a plan totalling $2,400 a year. The playbook also carries no play for a prospect with a hard, stated budget ceiling well under the offer.

notes: First call on the offer, and the process shows it: discovery gathered facts competently but never got past the goal list into why-now or consequence, so when $6,000 landed there was nothing holding it up. Coach the OC play end to end — isolate, HOW-not-SHOULD, then the full financial picture — before any lower-priced product is allowed on the table, and require that the tier presented actually beats the prospect's stated ceiling.
